newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks standing still at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks standing still at open.

text.p: The Australian share market was barely moved at the open on Friday with few traders interested as they awaited economic data, both locally and in the U.S.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index added 0.8 points to 2,486.2.
Local March retail trade figures are due at (0130 GMT), while Wall Street faces April employment figures later today.

"There is not too much happening. It was a little easier to start with but is firming up now. The volumes are not big," said dealer Brett O'Donovan of Brisbane brokerage, Lance Jones, adding that dramatic moves were unlikely ahead of the weekend with major U.S. data due.
"They are not going to push it one way or the other too much today." Local retail data was already seen largely priced in.
"If anything, the impact will be on the retail stocks. A lot of it is already factored in," O'Donovan said.
CRA rode sibling RTZ Plc's coat-tails higher after agreement with Aboriginal groups over the Century Zinc project in North Queensland was announced late on Thursday.
CRA shares were up 21 to A$19.24 before easing back to A$19.16 by 0045 GMT.
Overall, rises and falls were level pegging, while about 47 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
